title: OffSec OSWE
summary: OffSec OSWE, the Web Expert certification, is an advanced hands-on credential for people who audit and attack web applications at source code level. It suits web developers moving into security, application security engineers, and penetration testers who want to go beyond black box testing. The exam is a practical, proctored challenge in which you receive applications with their source code, review that code to find vulnerabilities, and then exploit each finding to prove real impact. There is no multiple choice section. OffSec does not publish per domain weightings for this exam, so the chapter list below gives the official domain names without percentages. Passing proves to an employer that you can read unfamiliar code, trace untrusted input to a dangerous function, and write a working exploit, and it leads to roles such as application security engineer, secure code reviewer, and senior web penetration tester. The domain structure below follows the published objectives; check the vendor's current version before booking.

beginner.definition: OSWE is an advanced certification from OffSec about web application security. A web application is software you reach through a browser, such as a shopping site or an internal tool. This certification is different from most because you receive the source code, which is the human readable program text. You read that code to find security bugs, then prove each bug is real by exploiting it.
beginner.whyItMatters: Automated scanners miss many serious bugs that only code review can reveal. This certification proves you can find those bugs yourself. An employer sees that you can join a development team and improve security before release, not only after. It supports well paid application security roles. It also makes you a sharper tester. You learn why an input is dangerous, not just which string triggers an alert.
howItWorks: Learn one server side language well, such as Java, PHP, or a JavaScript runtime, because you must read code.
Study the main vulnerability classes: injection, authentication flaws, and unsafe data handling.
Set up the sample applications in your own lab and trace how a request flows through the code.
Practise turning each weakness into a working exploit, so you can show genuine impact rather than a warning.
Rehearse with a timer, because the exam gives you a fixed period and several applications to attack.
The exam is proctored and practical. You review source code, exploit what you find, and submit a report.
beginner.example: Picture a mail room where every parcel is checked at the front desk. Attackers cannot smuggle anything past that desk. But the staff never check the internal envelopes that travel between departments. A code reviewer looks for those internal envelopes. They are the places where the program trusts data it should not trust. OffSec OSWE asks you to find one of those internal envelopes. You then prove that you can reach the vault.
takeaways: You must read code well. Pick one web language and study it properly first.
A warning is not a finding. You must exploit each bug to prove real impact.
OffSec does not publish domain weights here, so build your own study plan around weak areas.

objectives: Read an unfamiliar web application code base and map its entry points
Identify the exact places where untrusted input reaches a dangerous operation
Recognise authentication and session handling flaws from source code alone
Assess injection and deserialisation weaknesses in server side code
Build a working exploit that proves the real world impact of each finding
Explain root cause and remediation to a development team in plain language

chapters.title: Source code analysis for web applications
objectives: Read a web application code base and identify its routes and entry points
Trace data from a user request to the function that processes it
Spot missing validation and unsafe assumptions in server side code
Use debugging and logging to confirm how a suspected flaw behaves at runtime

chapters.title: Authentication and session security weaknesses
objectives: Review login and password reset logic for flaws that allow account takeover
Assess how sessions are created, stored, and validated
Identify privilege and role checks that can be bypassed
Exploit a weakness in this area to prove that unauthorised access is possible

chapters.title: Data handling and injection weaknesses
objectives: Find injection flaws where user input becomes part of a command or query
Recognise unsafe file handling, including upload, path, and template cases
Assess deserialisation of untrusted data and explain why it is dangerous
Build an exploit for an injection flaw that reaches a useful outcome

chapters.title: Custom exploits for web applications and APIs
objectives: Write a custom exploit script rather than relying on a ready made tool
Chain several smaller flaws into a single higher impact attack
Test an application programming interface for the same flaws as the web front end
Document each exploit so another engineer can reproduce it from your notes
